abstract: The HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein (Env) mediates host cell entry through interactions with CD4 and either coreceptor CCR5 or CXCR4 and is the target for neutralizing antibodies. During infection, some clade B viruses evolve from a CCR5- to CXCR4-using phenotype, a transition associated with accelerated AIDS progression. The mechanisms driving this coreceptor expansion remain poorly understood. Env regions involved in CCR5/CXCR4 interactions overlap with the N332/V3 epitope targeted by broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) suggesting antibody pressure could influence coreceptor expansion. Here, we use single genome amplification (SGA) to study Env evolution over 250 weeks in an HIV-infected individual from the SPARTAC Trial who develops an N332/V3 bnAb response and subsequently undergoes a coreceptor expansion. We show that Env mutations that facilitate coreceptor expansion overlap with those mediating escape from the host neutralizing antibody response, supporting a role for N332/V3 bnAbs in the emergence of X4-tropic Envs in this individual.

summary: Tracks HIV-1 Env evolution over 250 weeks in one SPARTAC participant, linking N332/V3 bnAb escape to CCR5-to-CXCR4 coreceptor expansion.
title: Coreceptor expansion in an HIV-1 infected individual with an N332/V3 broadly neutralizing antibody response.
